name: Fasta
summary: Generate three DNA sequences in FASTA format: a repeated ALU string and two weighted random sequences from a linear congruential generator.

spec.description: The Computer Language Benchmarks Game program, sequential. It cycles through a fixed string, draws weighted random symbols with an integer generator and a double-precision cumulative lookup, and formats everything into 60-character lines: string handling, a little floating point and lots of buffered output.
spec.input: Exactly one argument N made only of ASCII digits (leading zeros allowed), with 0 ≤ N ≤ 25000000.
spec.output: Three FASTA records, each a header line followed by its sequence wrapped at 60 characters per line (the last line may be shorter, every line ends with \n, no empty lines): '>ONE Homo sapiens alu' with the 287-character ALU string repeated cyclically for 2N characters; '>TWO IUB ambiguity codes' with 3N random IUB symbols; '>THREE Homo sapiens frequency' with 5N random Homo sapiens symbols. Exit code 0.
rules: One generator for the whole run, seed = 42: each random character does seed = (seed * 3877 + 29573) mod 139968, then r = seed / 139968.0 as an IEEE-754 double division. Record THREE continues from the state record TWO left.

Cumulative probabilities are the running double sum of the table probabilities in table order (starting from 0.0). Pick the first entry whose cumulative probability is greater than r; if there is none, the last entry.
Exactly one generator step per random character; no tables precomputed per seed value. A linear scan or the standard library's binary search over the cumulative table are both allowed.
Missing or extra arguments, non-digit characters or N > 25000000: usage message on stderr, nothing on stdout, exit code 1.
